records.source: וּבֹ֨עַז עָלָ֣ה הַשַּׁעַר֮ וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שָׁם֒ וְהִנֵּ֨ה הַגֹּאֵ֤ל עֹבֵר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּר־בֹּ֔עַז וַיֹּ֛אמֶר ס֥וּרָה שְׁבָה־פֹּ֖ה פְּלֹנִ֣י אַלְמֹנִ֑י וַיָּ֖סַר וַיֵּשֵֽׁב׃
records.gloss: And Boaz went up [to] the gate and sat there, and look, the redeemer [was] passing by, of whom had spoken Boaz; and he said, turn aside, sit here, a certain one, a certain one; and he turned aside and sat.
pieces: Meanwhile Boaz had gone up to the town gate and taken a seat there. Just then the family redeemer Boaz had spoken about came by. Boaz called to him, "Come over here and sit down, Mr. So-and-so." So the man came over and sat down.

L.1: Now Boaz had gone up to the gate and sat down there. And look, the redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken was passing by. And he said, "Turn aside, sit down here, Mr. So-and-so." And he turned aside and sat down.

R.1: Boaz went up to the town gate and sat down there. Soon the family redeemer Boaz had talked about came walking by. Boaz said, "Come over here, Mr. So-and-so, and sit down." So the man came and sat down.

decisions.choice: went up to the gate: the public place where town business was settled
decisions.reason: Bethlehem stood on a hill, so one went "up" to its gate. The gate was where people passed and met, and where the elders heard cases and witnessed agreements (Deuteronomy 25:7; Amos 5:15). Boaz goes there to settle Ruth's matter in public, as he promised (3:13). The Hebrew word order puts Boaz first, picking up the story while Ruth and Naomi wait (3:18).

decisions.choice: a certain one, a certain one: a stand-in for a name the storyteller does not give
decisions.reason: The pair of rhyming words is used when a speaker or writer chooses not to name a person or place (1 Samuel 21:3; 2 Kings 6:8). Boaz surely used the man's name; the narrator leaves it out. The man who will not keep up the dead man's name (verse 6) is himself left without a name in the story.

decisions.choice: the redeemer: the nearer relative with the first right and duty to redeem
decisions.reason: This is the relative Boaz spoke of in 3:12-13, closer in kinship to Elimelech than Boaz himself. On the redeemer's duty, see 2:20 (Leviticus 25:25).

decisions.choice: Mr. So-and-so
decisions.reason: A playful English stand-in for a name, as the Hebrew pair is. "Friend" would make Boaz's words warm and lose the point that the man is not named (m2).

decisions.choice: family redeemer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "family redeemer" for the go'el, as throughout Ruth; Literal keeps "redeemer".

records.heading: Boaz acquires the land and marries Ruth

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֞ח עֲשָׂרָ֧ה אֲנָשִׁ֛ים מִזִּקְנֵ֥י הָעִ֖יר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁבוּ־פֹ֑ה וַיֵּשֵֽׁבוּ׃
records.gloss: And he took ten men from [the] elders of the city and said, sit here; and they sat.
pieces: Then Boaz took ten men from the elders of the town and said, "Please sit down here." And they sat down.

L.2: And he took ten men from the elders of the town and said, "Sit down here." And they sat down.

R.2: Then Boaz chose ten of the town leaders. He asked them, "Will you sit down here?" So they sat down.

decisions.choice: ten men of the elders: enough witnesses to make the agreement binding
decisions.reason: The elders were the older men who led the town and judged its cases at the gate (Deuteronomy 25:7). Boaz gathers ten of them so that what is agreed is witnessed and cannot later be denied (verses 9-11).

decisions.choice: town leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "town leaders" for "elders", as at Deuteronomy 25:7. Literal and Balanced keep "elders".

decisions.choice: Please sit down / Will you sit down?
decisions.reason: Boaz is asking respected men to serve as a court. Balanced and Readable make the request polite; the Hebrew simply says "sit here".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לַגֹּאֵ֔ל חֶלְקַת֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאָחִ֖ינוּ לֶאֱלִימֶ֑לֶךְ מָכְרָ֣ה נָעֳמִ֔י הַשָּׁ֖בָה מִשְּׂדֵ֥ה מוֹאָֽב׃
records.gloss: And he said to the redeemer, [the] portion of the field which [was] to our brother, to Elimelech, is selling Naomi, who has returned from [the] country of Moab.
pieces: Then he said to the family redeemer, "Naomi, who has come back from the country of Moab, is putting up for sale the plot of land that belonged to our relative Elimelech.

L.3: Then he said to the redeemer, "The portion of the field that belonged to our brother Elimelech, Naomi, who has returned from the country of Moab, is selling.

R.3: Then Boaz said to the family redeemer, "Naomi has come back from Moab. She is selling the piece of land that belonged to our relative Elimelech.

decisions.choice: is selling: Naomi is putting the land up for sale now
decisions.reason: The verb form can mean "has sold" or describe an act being done as the words are spoken: "is selling". Since the redeemer is now asked to buy it (verse 4), the land is on offer. Some take it as "has sold": Naomi had earlier sold the use of the land, perhaps when the family left for Moab, and the redeemer would buy it back (Leviticus 25:25).

decisions.choice: our brother: our kinsman
decisions.reason: "Brother" is used here of a relative in the wider family, as often (Genesis 13:8). Elimelech belonged to the same clan as Boaz and the nearer redeemer (2:1, 3).

decisions.choice: the portion of the field: the family's share of the land
decisions.reason: Each family in Israel held a share of the land as its inheritance, to be kept within the family (Leviticus 25:23-25; Numbers 27:8-11). This is the first time the story says Elimelech's family owned land at Bethlehem.

decisions.choice: our relative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "relative" for "brother" so readers do not think Elimelech was the brother of both men (m2).

records.source: וַאֲנִ֨י אָמַ֜רְתִּי אֶגְלֶ֧ה אָזְנְךָ֣ לֵאמֹ֗ר קְ֠נֵה נֶ֥גֶד הַֽיֹּשְׁבִים֮ וְנֶ֣גֶד זִקְנֵ֣י עַמִּי֒ אִם־תִּגְאַל֙ גְּאָ֔ל וְאִם־לֹ֨א יִגְאַ֜ל הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י וְאֵֽדְעָה֙ כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין זוּלָֽתְךָ֙ לִגְא֔וֹל וְאָנֹכִ֖י אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָנֹכִ֥י אֶגְאָֽל׃
records.gloss: And I said, I will uncover your ear, saying, acquire [it] before those sitting and before [the] elders of my people; if you will redeem, redeem, and if not he will redeem, tell me so that I may know, for there is not except you to redeem, and I [am] after you. And he said, I will redeem.
pieces: I thought I should tell you about it and say, 'Buy it in the presence of those sitting here and of the elders of my people.' If you are willing to redeem it, then do so. If you are not, tell me, so that I know. For no one has the right to redeem it except you, and I come next after you." "I will redeem it," he said.

L.4: And I said I would uncover your ear, saying, 'Acquire [it] before those sitting [here] and before the elders of my people.' If you will redeem [it], redeem [it]; but if he will not redeem [it], tell me, so that I may know, for there is no one except you to redeem [it], and I [am] after you." And he said, "I will redeem [it]."

R.4: I thought I should let you know. You can buy it now, in front of these people sitting here and the leaders of my people. If you want to buy it back for the family, do it. But if you do not, tell me so that I know. You have the first right to buy it, and I am next after you." The man said, "I will buy it back."

decisions.choice: uncover your ear: tell you, let you know
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures moving aside hair or a head covering to speak privately into someone's ear. It means to inform someone (1 Samuel 20:2; 2 Samuel 7:27).

decisions.choice: if he will not redeem: Boaz means the redeemer himself
alternatives: if you will not redeem (some manuscripts and ancient versions)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "he" here, though Boaz is speaking to the man. Boaz may turn for a moment to the elders and speak of him, or the word may be a slip in copying. A number of Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient Greek, Syriac and Latin translations read "you". Either way the one who might refuse is the nearer redeemer.

decisions.choice: no one except you, and I after you: the order of kinship
decisions.reason: The right to redeem passed to the nearest relative first, then to the next (Leviticus 25:48-49). The nearer relative must take up the right or give it up before Boaz can act (3:12-13).

decisions.choice: those sitting: the people seated at the gate
decisions.reason: The word can mean "those sitting" or "the inhabitants". Here it is most naturally the people sitting at the gate (verse 9 speaks of "all the people"), set beside the ten elders.

decisions.choice: you will not
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "you", since Boaz is talking to the man (m2). Literal keeps the Hebrew "he".

decisions.choice: buy it back for the family
decisions.reason: Readable explains "redeem" as buying land back for the family, as Leviticus 25:25 describes.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר בֹּ֔עַז בְּיוֹם־קְנוֹתְךָ֥ הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה מִיַּ֣ד נָעֳמִ֑י וּ֠מֵאֵת ר֣וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֤ה אֵֽשֶׁת־הַמֵּת֙ קָנִ֔יתָה לְהָקִ֥ים שֵׁם־הַמֵּ֖ת עַל־נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Boaz, on [the] day you acquire the field from [the] hand of Naomi, and from Ruth the Moabite, [the] wife of the dead, you acquire [her], to raise up [the] name of the dead over his inheritance.
pieces: Then Boaz said, "On the day you buy the field from Naomi, and from Ruth the Moabite, the dead man's widow, you acquire Ruth as well, to keep the dead man's name alive on his inheritance."

L.5: Then Boaz said, "On the day you acquire the field from the hand of Naomi and from Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the dead [man], you acquire [her], to raise up the name of the dead [man] on his inheritance."

R.5: Then Boaz said, "When you buy the field from Naomi, you are also buying it from Ruth the Moabite, the dead man's widow. And you must take Ruth as your wife. Then the dead man's family name will live on with his land."

decisions.choice: you acquire: the form read aloud in the Hebrew tradition
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text read "I acquire"; the Masoretes' marginal reading, followed here, is "you acquire". With "you", Boaz tells the redeemer that buying the field brings with it the duty to marry Ruth. With "I", Boaz announces that he himself will marry Ruth whatever the other man does, which also explains why the man then gives up the land (verse 6).

decisions.choice: and from Ruth: the purchase involves Ruth too, and the buyer takes her as wife
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "and from Ruth". Ruth, as the widow of Mahlon, Elimelech's heir, has a share in the land's future, so the field cannot be bought without her. The words that follow, "you acquire, to raise up the name of the dead", show that the buyer takes Ruth as his wife (verse 10). A very small change in the Hebrew letters would give "you acquire also Ruth", the same sense.

decisions.choice: raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance: give the dead man an heir to hold his land
decisions.reason: A son born to Ruth would count as Mahlon's son and keep his name and his share of the land in Israel, as the law of Deuteronomy 25:5-6 intends. The land would then not stay with the buyer's own family.

decisions.choice: widow
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "widow" for "wife of the dead man", since her husband has died; Literal keeps "wife".

decisions.choice: you must take Ruth as your wife
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "acquire" means for Ruth (verse 10).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַגֹּאֵ֗ל לֹ֤א אוּכַל֙ לִגְאָל־לִ֔י פֶּן־אַשְׁחִ֖ית אֶת־נַחֲלָתִ֑י גְּאַל־לְךָ֤ אַתָּה֙ אֶת־גְּאֻלָּתִ֔י כִּ֥י לֹא־אוּכַ֖ל לִגְאֹֽל׃
records.gloss: And said the redeemer, not I am able to redeem for myself, lest I ruin my inheritance; redeem for yourself, you, my right of redemption, for not I am able to redeem.
pieces: The family redeemer replied, "Then I cannot redeem it for myself, or I would ruin my own inheritance. You take over my right of redemption yourself, for I cannot redeem it."

L.6: And the redeemer said, "I am not able to redeem [it] for myself, lest I ruin my own inheritance. Redeem my right of redemption for yourself, you, for I am not able to redeem [it]."

R.6: The family redeemer answered, "Then I cannot buy it back. If I did, I would put my own family's land at risk. You buy it back yourself. I give you my right to do it, because I cannot."

decisions.choice: lest I ruin my own inheritance: the cost would harm his own family
decisions.reason: He would pay for the field, and also support Ruth and her son, but the field would go to that son as Mahlon's heir, not to his own children. A son by Ruth might even claim a share of his own estate. What he could gladly buy for himself (verse 4) becomes a loss when it must be held for another man's name.

decisions.choice: my right of redemption: the right and duty that falls to him as nearer relative
decisions.reason: He hands it over to Boaz, who is next in line (verse 4). The same word is used in Leviticus 25:24 for the right to buy back land.

decisions.choice: to redeem: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew letters and the marginal reading differ slightly in the form of this verb; both mean "to redeem".

decisions.choice: Then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "Then" to show that the man answers because of what Boaz has just told him about Ruth (verse 5).

records.source: וְזֹאת֩ לְפָנִ֨ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל עַל־הַגְּאוּלָּ֤ה וְעַל־הַתְּמוּרָה֙ לְקַיֵּ֣ם כָּל־דָּבָ֔ר שָׁלַ֥ף אִ֛ישׁ נַעֲל֖וֹ וְנָתַ֣ן לְרֵעֵ֑הוּ וְזֹ֥את הַתְּעוּדָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And this [was] formerly in Israel concerning the redemption and concerning the exchange, to confirm every matter: drew off a man his sandal and gave [it] to his neighbor; and this [was] the attestation in Israel.
pieces: In earlier times in Israel, this was how redemption and exchange were made final: one man took off his sandal and gave it to the other. This was how an agreement was witnessed in Israel.

L.7: Now this [was the custom] formerly in Israel concerning redemption and concerning exchange, to confirm any matter: a man drew off his sandal and gave [it] to his neighbor. And this [was] the [way of] attesting in Israel.

R.7: Long ago in Israel, there was a custom when people bought back land or traded something. To make the deal final, one man took off his sandal and gave it to the other. That was how people in Israel showed that an agreement was settled.

decisions.choice: a man drew off his sandal and gave it: a sign of handing over a right
decisions.reason: A sandal was used in giving up or handing over a right. Here the one who gives up his right takes off his own sandal and gives it to the one who receives it, and the handing over is seen by witnesses. Deuteronomy 25:9 is a different use of the same sign: there a widow pulls the sandal off a man who refuses his duty, to shame him. The nearer redeemer in Ruth is not shamed; he gives up his right openly and freely.

decisions.choice: this was formerly in Israel: the narrator explains an old custom
decisions.reason: The storyteller steps out of the scene to explain a custom his readers no longer knew. This shows that the book was written down some time after the days it describes (1:1).

decisions.choice: redemption and exchange: buying back and trading
decisions.reason: "Redemption" is buying back family land or persons (Leviticus 25:24-26); "exchange" is any trade of property or rights (Leviticus 27:10).

decisions.choice: [was the custom], [way of]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies a noun for the bare "this was" so the sentence can be read.

decisions.choice: bought back land or traded something
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two terms (m3).

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַגֹּאֵ֛ל לְבֹ֖עַז קְנֵה־לָ֑ךְ וַיִּשְׁלֹ֖ף נַעֲלֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said the redeemer to Boaz, acquire [it] for yourself; and he drew off his sandal.
pieces: So when the family redeemer said to Boaz, "Buy it for yourself," he took off his sandal.

L.8: So the redeemer said to Boaz, "Acquire [it] for yourself." And he drew off his sandal.

R.8: So the family redeemer said to Boaz, "You buy it." And he took off his sandal and gave it to Boaz.

decisions.choice: he drew off his sandal: the nearer redeemer, giving it to Boaz
decisions.reason: The one who speaks is the one who takes off his sandal, following the custom just explained (verse 7). The Hebrew does not say that he gave it to Boaz; the ancient Greek translation adds "and gave it to him", and verse 7 implies it.

decisions.choice: and gave it to Boaz
decisions.reason: Readable completes the custom from verse 7 (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז לַזְּקֵנִ֜ים וְכָל־הָעָ֗ם עֵדִ֤ים אַתֶּם֙ הַיּ֔וֹם כִּ֤י קָנִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֶֽאֱלִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְכִלְי֖וֹן וּמַחְל֑וֹן מִיַּ֖ד נָעֳמִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Boaz to the elders and all the people, witnesses [are] you today that I acquire all that [was] to Elimelech and all that [was] to Chilion and Mahlon from [the] hand of Naomi.
pieces: Then Boaz said to the elders and all the people, "Today you are witnesses that I am acquiring from Naomi everything that belonged to Elimelech and everything that belonged to Chilion and Mahlon.

L.9: And Boaz said to the elders and all the people, "You [are] witnesses today that I acquire all that belonged to Elimelech and all that belonged to Chilion and Mahlon from the hand of Naomi.

R.9: Then Boaz spoke to the leaders and all the people there. "Today you have seen this," he said. "I am buying from Naomi all the land and goods that belonged to Elimelech and his sons, Chilion and Mahlon.

decisions.choice: you are witnesses today: a formal public declaration
decisions.reason: Boaz states the terms aloud before the court, so that the sale stands in law. The people answer, "Witnesses!" (verse 11). Compare Joshua 24:22.

decisions.choice: I acquire: the deal is done as he says it
decisions.reason: The verb form describes an act completed by being spoken, like "I hereby acquire".

decisions.choice: all that belonged to: the land and whatever went with it
decisions.reason: Elimelech's property would have passed to his sons; now both are dead (1:3-5), and it is in Naomi's hand. Chilion is named before Mahlon here, unlike 1:2, 5.

decisions.choice: all the land and goods; his sons
decisions.reason: Readable says what "all that belonged" includes and reminds readers who Chilion and Mahlon were.

decisions.choice: you have seen this
decisions.reason: Readable puts "you are witnesses" in everyday words.

records.source: וְגַ֣ם אֶת־ר֣וּת הַמֹּאֲבִיָּה֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת מַחְל֜וֹן קָנִ֧יתִי לִ֣י לְאִשָּׁ֗ה לְהָקִ֤ים שֵׁם־הַמֵּת֙ עַל־נַ֣חֲלָת֔וֹ וְלֹא־יִכָּרֵ֧ת שֵׁם־הַמֵּ֛ת מֵעִ֥ם אֶחָ֖יו וּמִשַּׁ֣עַר מְקוֹמ֑וֹ עֵדִ֥ים אַתֶּ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And also Ruth the Moabite, [the] wife of Mahlon, I acquire for myself for a wife, to raise up [the] name of the dead over his inheritance, and not will be cut off [the] name of the dead from with his brothers and from [the] gate of his place; witnesses [are] you today.
pieces: I am also acquiring Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon's widow, to be my wife, so that the dead man's name may be kept alive on his inheritance and not be cut off from among his relatives or from the gate of his hometown. Today you are witnesses."

L.10: And also Ruth the Moabite, the wife of Mahlon, I acquire for myself as a wife, to raise up the name of the dead [man] on his inheritance, so that the name of the dead [man] will not be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his place. You [are] witnesses today."

R.10: And I am taking Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon's widow, to be my wife. Then Mahlon's family name will live on with his land. His name will not be forgotten among his relatives or in his hometown. You have all seen this today."

decisions.choice: I acquire as a wife: marriage as part of a legal agreement
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for the field and for Ruth, because both were part of one agreement. It does not mean Ruth was bought as property; she had chosen Boaz (3:9-10), and the marriage keeps the promise he made her (3:13).

decisions.choice: the name will not be cut off from his brothers and from the gate of his place: he will not be forgotten in his family or his town
decisions.reason: "The gate of his place" is the town where he belonged, its public life gathered at the gate. A man without an heir would vanish from his clan's records and land; Boaz's marriage keeps Mahlon's line in Bethlehem (Deuteronomy 25:6).

decisions.choice: Ruth the Moabite: a foreign woman received into Israel
decisions.reason: Boaz names her as a Moabite in the public record. A law barred Moabites from the LORD's assembly (Deuteronomy 23:4), yet Ruth, who chose Naomi's people and God (1:16), becomes the wife of a leading man of Judah and an ancestor of David (verse 17).

decisions.choice: relatives; hometown
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "relatives" for "brothers" (as in verse 3) and "hometown" for "the gate of his place".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ כָּל־הָעָ֧ם אֲשֶׁר־בַּשַּׁ֛עַר וְהַזְּקֵנִ֖ים עֵדִ֑ים יִתֵּן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶֽת־הָאִשָּׁ֜ה הַבָּאָ֣ה אֶל־בֵּיתֶ֗ךָ כְּרָחֵ֤ל׀וּכְלֵאָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּנ֤וּ שְׁתֵּיהֶם֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַעֲשֵׂה־חַ֣יִל בְּאֶפְרָ֔תָה וּקְרָא־שֵׁ֖ם בְּבֵ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: And said all the people who [were] at the gate and the elders, witnesses; may make YHWH the woman, the [one] coming into your house, like Rachel and like Leah, who built [the] two of them [the] house of Israel; and make strength in Ephrathah and proclaim [a] name in Bethlehem.
pieces: All the people at the gate and the elders answered, "We are witnesses. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make the woman who is coming into your home like Rachel and Leah, the two women who built up the family of Israel. May you thrive in Ephrathah and be renowned in Bethlehem.

L.11: And all the people who [were] at the gate, and the elders, said, "[We are] witnesses. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make the woman who is coming into your house like Rachel and like Leah, the two of whom built the house of Israel. And may you make strength in Ephrathah and proclaim a name in Bethlehem.

R.11: Then all the people at the gate and the town leaders said, "Yes, we have seen it. We pray that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make Ruth, who is coming into your home, like Rachel and Leah. Those two women gave Israel its whole family. May you grow strong and rich in Ephrathah, and may your name be famous in Bethlehem.

decisions.choice: like Rachel and like Leah, who built the house of Israel: the mothers of Jacob's sons
decisions.reason: Rachel and Leah, with their servants, bore the sons of Jacob, from whom the tribes of Israel came (Genesis 29:31-30:24; 35:16-18). "Build a house" means to give a man a family line, the very thing a husband's brother was to do for the dead (Deuteronomy 25:9). Rachel was buried on the way to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem (Genesis 35:19), so her name fits a blessing spoken there. Rachel is named first though Leah was the elder, perhaps because she was Jacob's loved wife and was linked with Bethlehem.

decisions.choice: make strength: prosper, gain standing and family
decisions.reason: The word chayil means strength, ability, wealth and worth. It was used of Boaz (2:1) and of Ruth (3:11). Here it is a wish that Boaz will flourish, above all in the family the marriage will bring.

decisions.choice: proclaim a name in Bethlehem: be famous there
decisions.reason: To have one's name "called" or "proclaimed" is to be well known and remembered. The women say the same of the child (verse 14). The phrase may also look ahead to the naming of a son.

decisions.choice: Ephrathah and Bethlehem: two names for the same town and its clan
decisions.reason: Ephrathah was the old name of Bethlehem or of its clan (Genesis 35:19; Micah 5:1); Elimelech's family were "Ephrathites from Bethlehem" (1:2). The two names stand side by side as in Micah 5:1.

decisions.choice: Ruth
decisions.reason: Readable names the woman the people mean.

decisions.choice: Yes, we have seen it; We pray that
decisions.reason: Readable puts the one-word answer "Witnesses" and the wish form "may" in everyday words.

records.source: וִיהִ֤י בֵֽיתְךָ֙ כְּבֵ֣ית פֶּ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָ֥ה תָמָ֖ר לִֽיהוּדָ֑ה מִן־הַזֶּ֗רַע אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ מִן־הַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And may be your house like [the] house of Perez, whom bore Tamar to Judah, from the offspring which will give YHWH to you from the young woman this.
pieces: Through the children {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives you by this young woman, may your family be like the family of Perez, the son Tamar bore to Judah."

L.12: And may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, through the offspring that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give you from this young woman."

R.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will give you children by this young woman. May they make your family like the family of Perez, the son Tamar had by Judah."

decisions.choice: the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah: an earlier widow who kept a dead man's line alive
decisions.reason: Tamar was left a childless widow, and Judah's family failed to give her a husband as custom required. She bore Perez and Zerah to Judah himself (Genesis 38). Like Ruth, she was a foreign woman who kept a family line from dying out. Perez's family became the leading clan of Judah, and Boaz belonged to it (verses 18-21; 1 Chronicles 2:4-5).

decisions.choice: this young woman: Ruth
decisions.reason: The word na'arah is used of a young woman not yet long married. Boaz had called Ruth a young woman when he first saw her (2:5), and he had spoken of the younger men she could have chosen (3:10).

decisions.choice: the offspring that the LORD will give you: children as the LORD's gift
decisions.reason: The people's blessing says that the child will come from the LORD, and the next verse says that he did (verse 13).

decisions.choice: the clause about children comes first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the gift of children before the comparison so the long sentence reads clearly in English. Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח בֹּ֤עַז אֶת־רוּת֙ וַתְּהִי־ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א אֵלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לָ֛הּ הֵרָי֖וֹן וַתֵּ֥לֶד בֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And took Boaz Ruth, and she became to him for a wife, and he went in to her, and gave YHWH to her conception, and she bore a son.
pieces: So Boaz took Ruth home, and she became his wife. He slept with her, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} let her conceive, and she gave birth to a son.

L.13: So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. And he went in to her, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave her conception, and she bore a son.

R.13: So Boaz married Ruth, and she became his wife. They came together as husband and wife, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made it possible for her to become pregnant. She gave birth to a son.

decisions.choice: the LORD gave her conception: the child is the LORD's doing
decisions.reason: Ruth had been married to Mahlon for about ten years with no child (1:4-5). The narrator seldom says that the LORD acts directly; here and in 1:6, when he gave his people food, he does. The people's prayer in verse 12 is answered at once.

decisions.choice: he went in to her: he had sexual relations with her
decisions.reason: This is the usual way of speaking of a man consummating a marriage (Genesis 29:23; 38:2).

decisions.choice: slept with her / came together as husband and wife
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the idiom means (m2); Literal keeps "went in to her".

records.source: וַתֹּאמַ֤רְנָה הַנָּשִׁים֙ אֶֽל־נָעֳמִ֔י בָּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֔ה אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֣א הִשְׁבִּ֥ית לָ֛ךְ גֹּאֵ֖ל הַיּ֑וֹם וְיִקָּרֵ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said the women to Naomi, blessed [be] YHWH, who not has caused to cease for you [a] redeemer today; and may be proclaimed his name in Israel.
pieces: The women said to Naomi, "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has not left you this day without a family redeemer! May his name be renowned in Israel.

L.14: And the women said to Naomi, "Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has not left you without a redeemer today. And may his name be proclaimed in Israel.

R.14: The women of the town said to Naomi, "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Today {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given you a family redeemer, so that you are not left without one. May this child become famous in Israel.

decisions.choice: a redeemer, and his name: the newborn child
decisions.reason: The women mean the child. He is the one who will keep the family's name and land and care for Naomi when she is old (verse 15). Some take "his name" to mean the LORD's name, but the next verse goes on speaking of the child, and verse 11 used the same wish of Boaz.

decisions.choice: the women to Naomi: the end answers the beginning
decisions.reason: The women of Bethlehem who asked "Is this Naomi?" when she came home empty and bitter (1:19-21) now bless the LORD with her. The story that began with the loss of her husband and sons ends with a son for her family.

decisions.choice: blessed be the LORD: praise and thanks to God
decisions.reason: When a person "blesses" God, it means to praise and thank him for what he has done, as in Genesis 24:27.

decisions.choice: Praise the LORD
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "Praise" for "blessed be" when the one blessed is God (m3).

decisions.choice: this child
decisions.reason: Readable names the child as the one meant (m1), a choice the decision marks uncertain.

records.source: וְהָ֤יָה לָךְ֙ לְמֵשִׁ֣יב נֶ֔פֶשׁ וּלְכַלְכֵּ֖ל אֶת־שֵׂיבָתֵ֑ךְ כִּ֣י כַלָּתֵ֤ךְ אֲֽשֶׁר־אֲהֵבַ֨תֶךְ֙ יְלָדַ֔תּוּ אֲשֶׁר־הִיא֙ ט֣וֹבָה לָ֔ךְ מִשִּׁבְעָ֖ה בָּנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he will be to you for a restorer of life and to sustain your old age, for your daughter-in-law who loves you has borne him, who she [is] better to you than seven sons.
pieces: He will renew your life and take care of you when you are old. For your daughter-in-law, who loves you and means more to you than seven sons, is the one who has given birth to him."

L.15: And he will be to you a restorer of life and a sustainer of your old age; for your daughter-in-law who loves you has borne him, she who [is] better to you than seven sons."

R.15: This child will give you new life and look after you when you grow old. His mother is your daughter-in-law, who loves you. She is better to you than seven sons!"

decisions.choice: a restorer of life: the answer to 1:21
decisions.reason: The words mean one who brings back a person's life or strength (Lamentations 1:16). Naomi had said that the LORD "brought me back empty" (1:21), using the same verb "bring back". Now the LORD has brought her life back.

decisions.choice: sustain your old age: provide for you when you are old
decisions.reason: The verb means to feed and support, as Joseph provided for his father's household (Genesis 47:12). An old widow without children had no one to depend on.

decisions.choice: better than seven sons: worth more than the fullest family
decisions.reason: Seven stands for completeness, and seven sons was a picture of perfect blessing for a mother (1 Samuel 2:5; compare 1 Samuel 1:8). Sons counted for much in that world; the women say Ruth's love is worth more than any number of them.

decisions.choice: His mother is your daughter-in-law
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long clause into short sentences and turns "has borne him" into "his mother".

records.source: וַתִּקַּ֨ח נָעֳמִ֤י אֶת־הַיֶּ֨לֶד֙ וַתְּשִׁתֵ֣הוּ בְחֵיקָ֔הּ וַתְּהִי־ל֖וֹ לְאֹמֶֽנֶת׃
records.gloss: And took Naomi the child and placed him in her bosom, and she became to him for a nurse.
pieces: Then Naomi took the child, laid him on her lap, and cared for him.

L.16: And Naomi took the child and laid him in her bosom, and became his nurse.

R.16: Naomi took the baby boy and held him close in her arms. She took care of him.

decisions.choice: nurse: one who looks after and brings up a child
decisions.reason: The word is not the usual word for a nursing mother. It is used of a man or woman who carries and cares for a child (Numbers 11:12; 2 Samuel 4:4; 2 Kings 10:1, 5). Naomi becomes the child's guardian.

decisions.choice: laid him in her bosom: holding him close as her own
decisions.reason: To hold a child to one's bosom shows love and care (2 Samuel 12:3; Numbers 11:12). Some see in the act a formal adoption of the child into Elimelech's family, but the text describes only the gesture.

decisions.choice: lap / arms; cared for him / took care of him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for "bosom" and say what "became his nurse" means (m1).

records.source: וַתִּקְרֶאנָה֩ ל֨וֹ הַשְּׁכֵנ֥וֹת שֵׁם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יֻלַּד־בֵּ֖ן לְנָעֳמִ֑י וַתִּקְרֶ֤אנָֽה שְׁמוֹ֙ עוֹבֵ֔ד ה֥וּא אֲבִי־יִשַׁ֖י אֲבִ֥י דָוִֽד׃פ
records.gloss: And called to him the neighbor women [a] name, saying, has been born [a] son to Naomi; and they called his name Obed; he [was the] father of Jesse, [the] father of David.
pieces: The women who lived nearby gave him a name. "Naomi has a son!" they said, and they called him Obed. He became the father of Jesse, David's father.

L.17: And the neighbor women gave him a name, saying, "A son has been born to Naomi." And they called his name Obed. He [was] the father of Jesse, the father of David.

R.17: The women who lived near Naomi named the boy. They said, "Naomi has a son!" They named him Obed. Obed grew up to be the father of Jesse, and Jesse was the father of King David.

decisions.choice: a son born to Naomi: the heir of her family
decisions.reason: Ruth bore the child, but as Mahlon's heir he belongs to the family of Elimelech and Naomi (verses 5, 10). The women speak of him as Naomi's son, the one who carries on her husband's line.

decisions.choice: Obed: "one who serves"
decisions.reason: The name comes from the verb "to serve" or "to worship". It may be short for a longer name such as Obadiah, "servant of the LORD".

decisions.choice: the neighbor women gave him a name: an unusual naming
decisions.reason: In the Bible the parents usually name a child (Genesis 30; 1 Samuel 1:20). Only here do the women of the neighborhood do it, as the town shares Naomi's joy. The "calling of a name" (verses 11, 14) now comes true.

decisions.choice: the father of Jesse, the father of David: where the story leads
decisions.reason: David's name is the last word of the verse. The loyalty of Ruth, Naomi and Boaz in the dark days of the judges (1:1) prepares the way for Israel's king. This is the first time David is named in the Bible.

decisions.choice: King David
decisions.reason: Readable adds "King" so young readers know who David is.

records.source: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ תּוֹלְד֣וֹת פָּ֔רֶץ פֶּ֖רֶץ הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־חֶצְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron;
pieces: These are the descendants of Perez. Perez fathered Hezron.

L.18: And these [are] the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron.

R.18: Here is the family line from Perez to David. Perez was Hezron's father.

decisions.choice: these are the generations of: the heading of a family record
decisions.reason: The same heading opens the family records of Genesis (Genesis 2:4; 5:1; 11:27; 25:19; 37:2). It sets the story of Ruth among the great family histories of Israel. The same line, from Perez to David, appears again in 1 Chronicles 2:4-15 and in Matthew 1:3-6, which takes it on to Jesus and names Tamar, Rahab and Ruth among the mothers.

decisions.choice: ten generations from Perez to David
decisions.reason: The list names ten men, from Perez to David, with Boaz in the seventh place. Ancient family lists often counted in such set patterns and could leave out names; the list traces the line, not every generation. Hezron went down to Egypt with Jacob (Genesis 46:12).

decisions.choice: from Perez to David
decisions.reason: Readable says at once where the list leads.

records.heading: The family line from Perez to David

records.source: וְחֶצְרוֹן֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־רָ֔ם וְרָ֖ם הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־עַמִּֽינָדָֽב׃
records.gloss: and Hezron fathered Ram, and Ram fathered Amminadab;
pieces: Hezron fathered Ram, and Ram fathered Amminadab.

L.19: And Hezron fathered Ram, and Ram fathered Amminadab.

R.19: Hezron was Ram's father, and Ram was Amminadab's father.

decisions.choice: Amminadab: a man of the time of the exodus
decisions.reason: Amminadab's daughter Elisheba married Aaron (Exodus 6:23). Ram is named in the same line in 1 Chronicles 2:9-10.

decisions.choice: Ram's father
decisions.reason: Readable says "was ... father" for "fathered" throughout this list (verses 18-22).

records.source: וְעַמִּֽינָדָב֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־נַחְשׁ֔וֹן וְנַחְשׁ֖וֹן הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־שַׂלְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmah;
pieces: Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon.

L.20: And Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmah.

R.20: Amminadab was Nahshon's father, and Nahshon was Salmon's father.

decisions.choice: Nahshon: leader of the tribe of Judah in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Nahshon son of Amminadab led Judah when Israel left Sinai and brought the first gift at the altar's dedication (Numbers 1:7; 2:3; 7:12; 10:14).

decisions.choice: Salmah: the same man as Salmon in verse 21
decisions.reason: The name is spelled Salmah here and Salmon in the next verse; 1 Chronicles 2:11 has Salma. The spellings are forms of one name.

decisions.choice: Salmon
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell the name Salmon, as in verse 21, so readers see one person; Literal keeps the spelling of this verse.

records.source: וְשַׂלְמוֹן֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־בֹּ֔עַז וּבֹ֖עַז הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־עוֹבֵֽד׃
records.gloss: and Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed;
pieces: Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed.

L.21: And Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed.

R.21: Salmon was Boaz's father, and Boaz was Obed's father.

decisions.choice: Salmon fathered Boaz: Rahab in the line
decisions.reason: Matthew 1:5 names Rahab, the woman of Jericho who sheltered Israel's spies (Joshua 2; 6:25), as the wife of Salmon and the mother of Boaz. Ruth's book does not mention her.

decisions.choice: Boaz fathered Obed: the son counted as Mahlon's heir is listed as Boaz's
decisions.reason: The child was to carry Mahlon's name and land (verse 10), yet the family line lists him as Boaz's son. Both were true: in law he was Mahlon's heir, and by birth he was Boaz's son.

records.source: וְעֹבֵד֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־יִשָׁ֔י וְיִשַׁ֖י הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־דָּוִֽד׃
records.gloss: and Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.
pieces: Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

L.22: And Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

R.22: Obed was Jesse's father, and Jesse was David's father.

decisions.choice: Jesse fathered David: the book ends with Israel's king
decisions.reason: The book closes on David's name, as verse 17 does. The LORD's care for one widowed family in Bethlehem was part of his care for all Israel, and for the line of the king through whom he would keep his promises (2 Samuel 7:12-16).
